preheader: Armadin raises $255.5M, WTA hits prize parity, and Nike announces job cuts.

lead.headline: Kevin Mandia’s Armadin secures $255.5 million at a $2.5 billion valuation
lead.body: Cybersecurity veteran Kevin Mandia is back with Armadin, a startup that uses agent swarms to test and protect enterprise networks. The company closed a massive Series B funding round backed by heavyweights like Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, and Bain Capital Ventures.
lead.why: If you are tracking venture capital or building a startup, this deal shows how immense investor appetite remains for autonomous AI agents in specialized B2B software sectors.

stories.headline: Nike cuts jobs as CEO Elliott Hill overhauls global operations
stories.body: Nike is cutting jobs and reorganizing its operating model as CEO Elliott Hill works to revive slumping sales, particularly in the crucial China market. Hill hopes the changes will make the apparel giant more agile and efficient.
stories.why: A classic corporate turnaround case study. Keep an eye on how sweeping leadership reorganizations impact brand positioning and operational margins in retail.

stories.headline: Broadcom's third-quarter revenue surges 86 percent on AI chip demand
stories.body: Broadcom continues to post robust revenue growth, driven largely by skyrocketing demand for its artificial intelligence semiconductors. An analyst report highlights the stock as it sets up for a potential breakout.
stories.why: A great benchmark for hardware monetization. It illustrates how traditional chipmakers successfully pivot their supply chains to capture high-margin AI infrastructure spending.

stories.headline: Samsung hikes Galaxy S26 prices by $100 amid persistent memory shortages
stories.body: Samsung has raised prices across most of its new Galaxy S26 smartphone lineup. Consumer tech brands are passing higher hardware costs onto buyers as the artificial intelligence boom strains global memory chip supplies.
stories.why: Shows how upstream component bottlenecks in data centers directly squeeze hardware margins and reshape consumer pricing power.

stories.headline: OpenAI adds virtual clothing try-on features to ChatGPT shopping
stories.body: OpenAI has rolled out a new feature allowing users to upload a selfie or full-body photo to virtually try on clothes and accessories. The tool appears as a try-on button inside ChatGPT shopping results.
stories.why: A fascinating product expansion into e-commerce UX. It demonstrates how generative AI layers directly onto consumer retail experiences to cut down return rates.

stories.headline: Accenture to slow fiscal 2027 hiring as AI boosts employee output
stories.body: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet announced that while the firm will keep hiring across all markets, the overall pace will drop compared to last year. Artificial intelligence-driven productivity gains are allowing the company to generate more revenue per employee.
stories.why: Directly impacts recruiting timelines for business services and consulting. Firms are scaling headcount more efficiently by using AI tools to handle heavy workloads.

stories.headline: UNM Lobos basketball set for December trip to UC Irvine
stories.body: College basketball scheduling reports indicate that the New Mexico Lobos will face UC Irvine on December 18 in what is shaping up to be a pivotal pre-conference matchup.

stories.headline: WTA announces equal prize money across all combined 1000 tournaments by 2027
stories.body: The Women's Tennis Association announced a major milestone, confirming that all combined WTA 1000 tournaments will award women equal prize money to the men starting in 2027, with the Italian Open among the events joining the parity push.

term.name: Series B Funding
term.definition: The second round of venture capital financing for a startup that has moved past the initial product development stage. At this point, companies like Armadin use the capital to scale operations, expand marketing, and grow their teams after proving their business model works.

serve.headline: Armadin raised $255.5M to scale its AI cybersecurity agent swarms
serve.body: Founded by Mandiant creator Kevin Mandia, the San Francisco-based startup builds autonomous security platforms to test and defend enterprise systems. Its outsized Series B round was co-led by top-tier venture firms including Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, and Bain Capital Ventures.
questions: How would you pitch an enterprise client on trusting autonomous AI agents with core security protocols?
With top-tier VCs crowding into cybersecurity, what is your differentiator if a competitor copies your agent swarm architecture?
How do you plan your cash burn when a $255.5 million war chest instantly raises investor expectations for growth velocity?
